assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: assert_published_inside_the_limit fails if the reading is published after the sweep step rather than at the head of the pass (the red arm measured 15.6 seconds against 8); the journal assertion fails if the sweep's completion row is not written before the pass ends it; assert not stale.exists() fails if the sweep never removes the entry.
assertion_review.independence: The latency is the difference between the test's own clock taken before the child starts and the utc the production pass wrote into its record; the journal rows are parsed from the file the production sweep wrote.
assertion_review.limit: The reading is compared against a clock taken before bash has started, so slow process startup is charged to the pass; the real reclaim work runs under the same 2-second step bound the case uses to demonstrate an overrun.

assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: The case fails if the pass aborts on the failing sample-test-processes step before reaching the sweep (journal empty), if the reading is published last (red arm: 13.8 seconds against 8), or if the reading record is left stale by the failed step.
assertion_review.independence: The journal and the published reading are production artefacts; the 'Permission denied' line is emitted by the test's own STUB_SHIM, so that assertion shows only that the step was invoked.
assertion_review.limit: The stub fails one step, so a pass that swallowed the failure silently would still satisfy the assertion set as long as it kept going and published.

assertion_review.conditions_for_failure: The assertion fails when the published crew_scratch census names the orphan as retained (removed falsy) after the sweep ran; it holds when the census omits the orphan row entirely.
assertion_review.independence: The census is read from the record production wrote, compared against the path the test created.
assertion_review.limit: A regression that stopped recording the removed entry at all passes this assertion, so it guards a retained row rather than a recorded removal.

findings.text: non-blocking: the restated census assertion is `not any(path == orphan and not removed)`, which passes vacuously when the published crew_scratch census carries no row for the orphan at all, so a sweep that stops stating its removal satisfies the assertion written to prove it states one; asserting the row is present with a truthy removed value would keep the crew scratch census as the record the comment claims it is.

non-blocking: sweep_case runs the real reclaim work under FLEET_STEP_BOUND_SECONDS = 2 (bin/fleet-health:213 applies that bound to reclaim-node-scratch) before the stub lingers, so on the loaded node this case is about the real sweep can be killed mid-journal and fail the completeness assertion for a reason the case is meant to exclude; give the real sweep a bound above its own work and below SWEEP_SLEEP.
